selection_rationale: The oldest selected primary among the screened records provides direct division observation and explicit recovery-stage counts; newer abstracts lacked that specific pedigree/exposure contract. No claim that no newer eligible experiment exists.

primary_source.inspection_depth: All80 body paragraphs, including main narrative, available Methods and embedded main-figure captions read; raw reads, supplementary tables/figures, movies and S5pipeline unacquired/unreplayed.

anchors.original_interpretation: Joint sequencing of subclones can assign branch variants to observed lineage segments; this is not an endpoint cell-count mutation estimator.
Two non-isogenic cell lines, HT115 POLE V411L colon carcinoma and telomerase-immortalized RPE1, each form a displayed lineage from one founder; imaging measures divisions.
Figure2 caption marks cells that died/unrecovered and sequenced subclones; HT115 collection141h and RPE1 collection168h do not create independent trials.
Branch variants require support in at least two subclones; inherited appearances are grouped into a lineage event rather than counted as separate births.
Sequencing-only lineage reconstruction reproduces relationships but lacks independent cell-division timing/counts supplied by optical imaging.
Results report branch-call sensitivity96.4%HT115 and91.9%RPE1, specificity99.9%; these are method-dependent internal estimates.
HT115 reported173SNVs/division and3.0e-8SNV/bp/division with source Poisson-model intervals; no source rate is refitted here.
RPE1 reported39SNVs/division,4.3e-9SNV/bp/division, and3.3e-9after modeled oxidation-signature subtraction; raw and adjusted estimates are different.
Observed branch counts poorly agree with homogeneous Poisson accrual; heterogeneity/correlations are relevant count-law alternatives.
Clustered adjacent variants can be nonindependent; a molecular lesion/episode need not equal one SNV call.
Founder choice and viability/recovery produce two possible selection stages; approximate survival30%HT115/65%RPE1 is reported separately from exact Methods stage counts.
The study states insufficient power to choose elapsed time versus division counts; no general power inference is transferred.
HT115 and RPE1 use different media and serum concentrations, reinforcing unmatched-background interpretation.
Time-lapse imaging every3min and recorded release/reseeding maintain lineage identity; independent exposure information is present in principle.
Exact source stage counts: HT11545channel/37isolated/11outgrown/11sequenced; RPE126channel/22isolated/15outgrown/13sequenced.
Copy-number analysis indicates HT115 largelydiploid and RPE1predominantlytriploid; effective genome lengths5.7e9/9.2e9bp differ.
First-division reference state needs an external genotype; an additional HT115 subclone from a different lineage is a reference, not a matched intervention arm.
Source explicitly lacks a sufficiently accurate independent validation method; call calibration uses consensus lineage consistency.
Methods formula reportsRPE1sensitivity0.918 versus Results91.9%; both source values are preserved without invented reconciliation.
Sequencing accessionSRP159787 and public code are declared; raw reads, supplemental code and branch tables are not replayed in this audit.
